pieces.t: The New Mexico Journeyman Electrician examination is part of the state electrical licensing and qualification process. The process may include application review, documentation of qualifying electrical experience or training, examination approval, and final credential issuance requirements. Journeyman-level electrical testing is designed to measure whether the candidate understands the electrical knowledge required to perform electrical work safely and correctly under applicable rules. Journeyman exam preparation focuses on practical trade knowledge, code application, wiring methods, safety, calculations, and the ability to apply NEC rules to real installation scenarios.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: New Mexico journeyman electrician preparation should include the National Electrical Code, electrical theory, practical installation knowledge, conductor sizing, grounding and bonding, services, feeders, branch circuits, motors, transformers, wiring methods, raceways, boxes, overcurrent protection, special occupancies, special equipment, safety, and calculations. Candidates should also be prepared to review New Mexico electrical rules, construction licensing requirements, permit-related responsibilities, and state-specific subjects when those topics are part of the exam or credential path. Electrical calculations are an important part of journeyman-level preparation. Candidates should practice service load calculations, feeder calculations, branch-circuit calculations, conductor ampacity, conductor adjustment and correction, voltage drop, box fill, raceway fill, motor calculations, transformer calculations, demand factors, neutral loads, continuous loads, and overcurrent protection sizing.

pieces.h: Q: Is the New Mexico electrical exam open book?
pieces.t: New Mexico electrical exam preparation should include open-book code navigation and reference-use practice. Candidates should follow the current New Mexico and PSI exam instructions for the exact references, tabs, notes, calculators, and code edition allowed during testing.

pieces.h: Q: Can I bring these books into the exam room?
pieces.t: Exam-room reference rules are controlled by the current candidate bulletin and testing instructions. Candidates should review the official rules before test day to confirm which books and materials are permitted.

pieces.h: Q: Why are NEC tabs helpful?
pieces.t: NEC tabs help candidates locate major articles, chapters, tables, and subject areas faster during study. This supports stronger code-navigation practice and helps candidates become more comfortable using the NEC as a reference.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package include calculation practice?
pieces.t: Yes. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is included to help candidates review calculation topics that commonly appear on master electrician, journeyman, qualifying party, and electrical contractor exams.

pieces.h: Q: Does a journeyman certificate automatically operate as an electrical contractor license?
pieces.t: No. Journeyman certification and contractor licensing are separate considerations. Candidates who plan to contract for electrical work should review New Mexico contractor licensing requirements and qualifying party rules.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package guarantee that I will pass?
pieces.t: No. This package is designed to support preparation through organized study materials, code review, calculations practice, flash cards, online questions, and structured study guidance. Exam results depend on the candidate’s preparation, knowledge, and performance.

pieces.h: Q: Should I confirm New Mexico licensing requirements before testing?
pieces.t: Yes. Candidates should confirm the required credential, classification, eligibility requirements, application process, code edition, reference rules, and post-exam licensing steps before scheduling or taking an exam.

pieces.h: Exam Room Approved Books
pieces.t: NFPA 70 – National Electrical Code or National Electrical Code Handbook The New Mexico PSI bulletin lists the National Electrical Code or National Electrical Code Handbook as an allowed reference for the EE-98 electrical examinations. Candidates should use the edition listed in the current PSI bulletin for their scheduled exam and follow all rules for binding, highlighting, underlining, indexing, tabs, written notes, and loose papers. New Mexico Electrical Code The New Mexico Electrical Code is listed as an allowed reference for EE-98 Part 1 and Part 2. It supports state-specific electrical code questions and should be prepared according to PSI’s reference-material rules. National Electrical Safety Code The National Electrical Safety Code is listed as an allowed reference for EE-98 Part 1 Commercial and Industrial. Candidates should bring only the edition allowed by the current PSI bulletin for the scheduled exam.

pieces.h: Exam Room Approved Books
pieces.t: NFPA 72 – National Fire Alarm Code NFPA 72 is listed as an allowed reference for EE-98 Part 3 Specialties, which includes low voltage, alarms, telephone, computer, sound, and communication systems.

pieces.h: Q: Is this combo based on the 2026 NEC?
pieces.t: Yes. This combo is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code and includes the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback.

pieces.h: Q: What books are included in this package?
pieces.t: This package includes the 2026 New Mexico Master Electrician Study Guide, the 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide, and the National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback.

pieces.h: Q: Who should use this New Mexico master electrician combo?
pieces.t: This combo is intended for electricians preparing for New Mexico master-level electrical, electrical contractor, journeyman, NEC-based, open-book code navigation, and electrical calculation exam content.

pieces.h: Q: Who administers New Mexico electrical licensing?
pieces.t: New Mexico electrical licensing is administered through the New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department, Construction Industries Division.

pieces.h: Q: Who provides New Mexico electrical exams?
pieces.t: PSI provides examination and licensing processing services for New Mexico construction licensing, including electrical examination paths.

pieces.h: Q: Does New Mexico use a master electrician license?
pieces.t: New Mexico electrical licensing is commonly organized around contractor classifications, journeyman classifications, qualifying party requirements, and specialty scopes. Candidates should confirm the exact license, certificate, or classification they need.

pieces.h: Q: Does this package help with electrical calculations?
pieces.t: Yes. The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is included to help candidates practice formulas, NEC table use, load calculations, conductor sizing, raceway fill, box fill, service calculations, and other calculation-based topics.

pieces.h: Q: Can I study directly from the NEC with this package?
pieces.t: Yes. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback is included so candidates can study article language, definitions, tables, exceptions, and code requirements directly.

pieces.h: Q: Who is this New Mexico Master Electrician exam prep combo for?
pieces.t: This combo is for electricians preparing for New Mexico master-level electrical exam preparation, EE-98 Residential and Commercial Electrical testing, or NEC-based electrical exam review who want a study guide, flash cards, 12 practice exams, and 2 full final exams in one structured preparation package.

pieces.h: Q: Is this product based on the 2026 National Electrical Code?
pieces.t: Yes. This product is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code and is designed to support NEC-focused electrical exam preparation.

pieces.h: Q: Does this product include practice exams?
pieces.t: Yes. This package includes 12 practice exams plus 2 full final exams. The practice exams help you build familiarity with exam-style questions, while the final exams help you evaluate readiness after completing more of your study plan.

pieces.h: Q: Are flash cards included?
pieces.t: Yes. This is a study guide and flash card combo. The flash cards are designed to help reinforce electrical terms, formulas, definitions, NEC concepts, New Mexico state code topics, calculations, and exam-style recall.

pieces.h: Q: Is the New Mexico EE-98 electrical exam open book?
pieces.t: Yes. The New Mexico EE-98 Residential and Commercial Electrical exams are open book tests. Candidates are responsible for bringing their own approved references and following PSI rules for binding, highlighting, underlining, indexing, tabs, writing, and prohibited papers.

pieces.h: Q: How many parts are in the New Mexico EE-98 exam?
pieces.t: The EE-98 Residential and Commercial Electrical examination is a three-part combination exam: Part 1 Commercial and Industrial, Part 2 Residential, and Part 3 Specialties.

pieces.h: Q: How many questions are on the New Mexico EE-98 exam?
pieces.t: Part 1 contains 80 questions, Part 2 contains 40 questions, and Part 3 contains 50 questions.

pieces.h: Q: What is the passing score for the New Mexico EE-98 electrical exam?
pieces.t: Each EE-98 exam part requires a 75% passing score.

pieces.h: Q: Does New Mexico require Business and Law for contractors?
pieces.t: Yes. Contractor candidates must either pass the PSI Business and Law examination or complete an approved Business and Law course.

pieces.h: Q: What references are allowed for the New Mexico EE-98 electrical exam?
pieces.t: Approved electrical references include the National Electrical Code and the New Mexico Electrical Code, NMAC 14.10.4. Business and Law references include the NASCLA Contractors Guide to Business, Law and Project Management, the New Mexico Construction Industries Licensing Act, and New Mexico contractor licensing requirement rules.

pieces.h: Q: Does this combo guarantee that I will pass the exam?
pieces.t: No. This product is designed to support preparation through structured study, practice exams, final exams, flash card review, reference navigation, and NEC-based preparation. Exam results and licensing approval depend on the candidate’s preparation, testing performance, and New Mexico licensing requirements.
